data: Amazing game, amazing story, amazing graphics
Best game in years definitely worth the money, amazing graphics and playstyle btw
The gameplay is amazing, voice acting is amazing, story telling is amazing, and the graphics are amazing
fantastic game, great voice acting, great story, great music
It's well worth it on sale
, sadly, they wasted it on a disappointing story
There's no interesting gameplay, this is just a walking simulator, a short film you go through in about 2 hours, and that's about it
I will not be playing through this game again, going through all the same boring motions just to experience the ending
unfortunately, I'm experiencing severe motion sickness, especially during Molly's story, making it impossible to continue
sadly not a story I could get behind at all
I don't have an opinion about the gameplay because there isn't much of it
If you are considering buying the game and you know you can get motion sickness, I'd suggest watching the gameplay on youtube instead
there's not much gameplay that you NEED to experience yourself
Here I am, trying to explain you what I've felt after playing this very unique game experience, but I just simply can't do it.
Hauntingly beautiful storytelling! One you don't want to miss, even if this genre is outside of what you usually play. Would recommend to wait unit there's a sale as it is only a 2-3 hour long game.

★★★★★ (5-star scale)

OMG I love coming across games that just surprisingly leave me in awe . This game was so incredibly beautiful. As you explore the property in first-person - both in the creaky old house and the outside estate - you uncover the stories of the family members that once lived there. Not only is the artwork breathtaking, but the overall story you get to piece together was sososo well-written. There were parts where I got teary-eyed, and others where I was in utter shock. The gameplay is super fun too, as you get to play in both the present and in the past as these characters’ stories are told. Although this game feels spooky, this is not a “horror” game. It genuinely felt so cozy to play. I recommend this to anyone who loves narrative-based exploration games that want a more eerie feel - especially for the fall season. I definitely see myself playing this again in the future! <3

I can't imagine a person And more importantly, I can't understand them — who wouldn't enjoy this short yet incredibly rich game, both in terms of gameplay variety and its story and characters. I simply don't want to understand them, because What Remains of Edith Finch is a tiny masterpiece.

I played this game in one sitting. Great short game that takes only a couple of hours. I really enjoyed wondering from room to room (backyard too) and finding out more to the story. Each room has things to discover and some hidden rooms. These types of games are my favorite to play. I hope more and more games come out like this. I highly recommend this game if you are into story telling games that are short.

Triennale Art Games x Gone Home = one of the; if not the best "walking simulator" experience I've played so far. Not quite as atmospheric or free-roaming as "Gone Home" but still a highly enjoyable, funny, tragic and deeply human, expertly told story nonetheless. The genre needed exactly this kind of originality and creativity to elevate itself, combining gameplay and storytelling in the most poignant way. 8.5 (+)/10

Playing this game feels like taking a moment to look closely at your own reflexion inside of a polished pearl.

A brief, but very contemplative experience.

Wow. I just finished my first play-through, and I'm still catching my breath. It's not often that a game leaves you needing to collect yourself emotionally. I already want to do it again and take more screenshots on the way, because the art design is simply beautiful.
It's not a long game (well, maybe 20% game, 80% interactive story), just a few hours, and sometimes the controls are annoyingly vague. But the atmosphere and the pacing are spot-on. The sequence on the swing is worth the price (or at least the price I paid in a sale) on its own.
Buy it. If you don't like it, you have no soul.

What Remains of Edith Finch is a true story rich and atmospheric game experience. You play the character of Edith as she explores her unusual family home and unravels the secrets and tragic fates of her family members. Each story is told from the first person perspective of that family member and each story ends with a twist - you are a witness to it all..... One of the best games I have ever played from this particular genre. Even though it is a relatively short playthrough, I find myself constantly comming back to it in my mind. The stories, the visuals, music, narration, mystery, puzzles are all really captivating and I keep wanting to replay my experience. Wonderfully executed. BIttersweet but warm ending wraps the game up perfectly. Play this game and see for yourself what remains of Edith FInch <3
Very good game! It was really entertaining and wonderful story. A few glitches if you play without a controller but overall 10/10 would recommend!

Not sure how I feel about this one. The story was intriguing at first but by the end it didn't really feel like there was some big mystery (with the exception of two people, who I'm still wondering about). The controls were a bit annoying and frustrating at some points. It was also extremely short and for the most part it didn't really feel like you were doing something. Also, a missed opportunity not having the family tree at the very end reflect that last revelation. :[

It's debatable whether a walking simulator is a game. But I don't recall any Pope requiring transformatively moving experiences to have a "you lose" screen.

The stories are engaging, well built, and well told. The characters are fascinating. The world is beautiful, and bumbling around in it isn't just a device to aid immersion, but actually part of helping the game tell its own story. The control mechanics are intuitive and sometimes even brilliant. (The highlight of course being the much-praised cannery section, where the "real world" controls are tedious, but necessary to avoid obstructing the much more interesting and complicated "imaginary world.")

The game pretty much exists only to say "don't be sad it's over, be glad it happened." It wants to say it in the most beautiful way it can. It wants you to feel it. Give it a shot.

A very sad story but a beautiful game. Just know it is not a Point and Click adventure, but more of a walking simulator that leads you to slowly unfolding the mystery of the Finch house.

Trigger warning and SPOILER ALERT: If you can't handle dead children, this game is not for you. That being said, this is not a horror game but it is definitely spooky.

iv been going threw a really hard time lately. This game helped me threw it, it was relaxing and a great game play. I really enjoyed the story line and the graphics. Completed all the achievements pretty easily as well. I dont know if its important but it was on sale when i got it.

Not perfect (nothing is) but it comes as close as you could get in this genre. The new leader to beat in its sector, it's pure ecstasy.

10/10 -- Flawless

Yes it is short. Yes the price is fairly high for a short game. Think of it as a rollercoaster. Have you ever waited in a 30 or 60 minute line for a three minute ride??? Is the thrill worth it? Must be, because we climb into that next line. Well, What Remains of Edith Finch is a 2 hour rollercoaster ride of emotions if you play it correctly. If you run through the story and do not reflect on stuff, WROEF or any game like it is not for you.

This is a very short game. I played through it and got essentially all achievements in two hours, yet it's one of the most unique and intriguing games I've ever had the pleasure of experiencing.

I was reluctant to play it at first, I mostly threw it into a larger purchase I made, but when I eventually played it this is the game I enjoyed the most.

It looks stunning even on my relatively low end PC, the story is wonderful yet tragic and I was perplexed for several hours after completing the game and I truly wish I could go back and experience it all again.

One thing you should know before purchase is that this is not like any other game you've ever played. It's more like a visual novel. There is zero difficulty and the achievements are easy as hell to get. I don't write this to discourage as I, who prefer rather difficult games enjoyed this game immensely, just as a small heads up.

In short: Buy the game. It's dirt cheap and worth every dollar.

I feel compelled to write a fe words about this game... or perhaps more of a visual novel, a beatifully told interacive strory. It guides you along its path at a slow but steady pace, letting you learn and experience the mysterious story of the Finch family. It's an about 2-3 hour substitute of a short novel or a movie, probably longer if you want the explore to find a bit more information and let the story and the beautiful visuals soak in. It can be as engaging for people watching you play as for you as the player, or I'd rather say person controlling the flow of the plot... Definitely recommended for a long evening.

this was such a beautiful game and left a mark on me. short story but definitely unforgettable. every room is someone we can never actually meet or know what happened fully but all characters were written beautifully. really enjoyed playing this game. i also love the soundtrack

Tragic and well-written game with an emotional story. Worth waiting for a sale to buy it, as the price is a little high for such a short game. It's worth noting that there are a few questions left unanswered by the end.

Valued at 2.5 Dear Esthers, maybe rough parity with Gone Home.

In the ever increasing mystery house inspection genre, this is one of the best. The player character explores their overly renovated childhood home andexperiences the life stories of her colorful family. Although the game controls player activity more tightly than Gone Home, the way each 'family member' segment plays out - from exploring their part of the house to experiencing their last moments at the house - keep you searching for more information about them and the house.

Although it generally pushes players in a certain direction it can be easy to get lost in certain areas. Each of the stories play with different mechanics and narrative styles, but their freshness is a bit soured on returning to walking slowly around rooms looking for hidden passages.

Bravo, Giant Sparrow, what a brilliant game! It's taken me this long to get round to playing this gorgeous piece of work, but it was worth the wait.

I loved the setting, the characters, the music and the themes. I feel that this story/these stories could have been told in any medium (Theatre, cinema, television, audio drama, literature...you name it) and it would have been just as impactful, because the writing is phenomenal.

How do you even start reviewing this game….I’ve always struggled with the concept of sibling loss so i knew this would hurt lol I just didn’t expect to be swallowed whole :(

Some of the stories will stay with me, others have clawed under my skin. Lewis’s story in particular is one of the most devastating things I’ve experienced in a while. It’s not just the story… it’s how it's told, how the mechanics mirror the disconnection and the slow surrender to daydreaming. It’s masterfully done, genuinely made me stop for a while and just sit in it.

The house itself is one of the most beautiful and lovingly crafted spaces I’ve ever seen in a game. Every inch tells you something : every photo, trinket, book or childhood toy. Even the wallpapers and color schemes feel alive. And as you move through it you begin to feel the weight of inherited grief…

I know people complain about the length of the game but i think it was perfect? Things unfolded naturally, you even forget that you’re reading Edith’s entries in her journal. The storytelling shifting constantly really helped with that : shapeshifting, daydreaming, taking photographs, reading a comic…no repetition, just one long unraveling of lives cut short.
Amazing story telling. This was whimsical, tragic, funny, and highly immersive. It felt like getting lost in a book.

The game is a walking simulator coupled with a series of well-designed mini games. It looks good and I liked the voice acting and the music. However, there was too little characterization for me to care about what happens to most of the family.

I got so angry at this game. It ended and I shut it down and was so heated about it, I hopped into my discord server and started trashing it.

But then I realized something...well....I realized a lot of things.

It did have an ending. Just not the ending I wanted. It left me with more questions than answers but I soon realized that it was exactly the point of the story. You get more focused on the "what" is happening to this family and not the overall tragedy of this poor girl's existence.

And that is why I got so upset. I got so enveloped and transported to Edith's life that I didn't want to leave it after a few short hours with her.

I want to know more, I want to feel more.

And that is a pure example of how video games are am artform and I am a firm believer that sometimes video games are the best way to tell a story. What Remains Of Edith Finch is a shining example of this case. I strongly don't believe it could get told any other way and capture your emotions better than how it is presented.

I commend the developers for a job well done. It won my heart over. My biggest regret is not playing it sooner. Thank you for the experience.

Beautiful to wander through, hard to believe, moody and fantastical. I enjoyed it and it stayed with me long after the end. Best for players who enjoy visual eye candy and a compelling storyline that asks you to suspend reality time and time again. It is unique and entertaining.

Thank you, Giant Sparrow! You gave this world the kind of game every soul need to play.
11/10. Marvellous gameplay with an unforgettable story and super great soundtrack.

This game touched my deepest emotions. I love it in every moment.

"If we lived forever, maybe we’d have time to understand things. But as it is, I think all we can do is open our eyes, and appreciate how strange and brief this all is."

Life is short,
Love your family more.

This game shows that unreal engine is not only capable of good graphics but awesome gameplay events.
Each section feels unique and awesome and horrifying at the same time.

Essentially a playable short story, and a good one. There's some clever use of different media and different control schemes, but no real difficulty -- the point is to watch the stories unfold. Some of them are fun, and some are haunting. It's less a solve-the-puzzle mystery and more of an exploration. The writing and voice acting are both well done.

One of the best aspects of this game is how much character information it puts into set design, and how well it evokes a particular place. The game is set on Orcas Island, and the look and feel of the Pacific Northwest is spot on. It took me about two hours to get through the whole game, and that included a lot of stopping to look at details of each room, read the book titles, etc.

Non-metaphorical advice: if you're stuck in a UI element, try moving backwards, even if it doesn't make sense in context. That was the only UI issue I had in the entire game.

Edith Finch is a hell of a game. It takes the Gone Home formula to a new level, often transporting you out of the house you're exploring into "memories" of lost family members. These stories are eclectic, but still feel cohesive.

If I were capable of feeling emotions I'd imagine I would have felt some. The Finch family has been through hell.

Highly recommended if you enjoy this genre of game.

This was the very first game I had ever bought off of steam, and I think it's my favorite story game of all time. I bought it in 2019 and have been replaying it almost every month for every year since. Amazing characters, storyline, and the graphics are great. The creativity in this story makes me emotional every time I play it, and I will always love looking back on this game and remembering the first time I played it, and how amazed I was.
It's fine. Unique, experimental. I did not find it terribly coherent or inspiring in any particular direction as an audience member, but I can see why it is hailed as an innovative use of the medium.

Absolutely gorgeous presentation. In terms of walking simulators, I felt sometimes that the movement around the house was a little janky, but the developers did do a pretty good job of keeping the player moving down the right path, it's just that sometimes the triggers for entering a new area weren't completely explicit or would misfire. The storytelling structure is fantastic, and the wildly varied presentation of each family member's story was truly amazing to experience - and it made the inevitable outcome of each story all the more devastating. This might be one of the best walking sims I've ever played, just in terms of how damn much it made me feel every minute I was playing it. 100% worth your time.

A first example of a walking simulator that shows you that it can tell you a story and share the autor's vision through something more than a pedestrian activity. Although there is still room for improvement with the gameplay/storytelling ideas, it's still a great game.
The story, characters, voice acting, sound and design are impeccable and provide a valuable experience.

It will not leave you indifferent after you complete it...

What Remains of Edith Finch is weird. Very, very weird. But not in a bad way at all. The game has some great lighting and while some areas may look a little dated, my overall consensus on the graphics are that they are good enough to be very immersive. The story itself is gripping and is constantly interesting, with each chapter feeling like an entirely different game. In one part I found myself playing two games at once, which I found really quite unique. The voice acting is also very strong, and strong emotion is displayed throughout the game.

While the game itself is short in length, around 2 hours long, the story is rich and compelling as each stage of the game feels new and refreshing. I was gripped for the entirety of the playthrough. I highly recommend this game to anyone who wants a incredibly unique gaming experience which I will never forget. This game is the complete package. If you haven't played it yet, you are missing out on an incredible experience.

I'm...I'm still in awe of the magnificence of this journey. What an emotional ride Edith Finch is. The storytelling in this game is second-to-none, and the variety of narratives makes this a true familial experience. What is family? What makes a family? What kinds of secrets do families keep? These questions--and more--lie at the heart of Edith Finch. It's not a long game, but you'll want to take it as slowly as you can. Experience the rich world the developers built and take every. single. moment. in. Don't worry if you miss something on your first playthrough, as you can go back and replay any chapters you wish once you complete the game. I can't recommend this game enough and will be talking about it for weeks. A must-buy.

Note: I did purchase this on sale. While it was well worth the sale price, I do think the full price is a little steep for such a short game. I'd suggest waiting for a sale before purchasing, but snap it up as soon as it happens.

I really beautiful and heavy game. 10/10 in terms of storyline. I did feel like a character in a movie where I had no say in what happens next or any gameplay where I was capable of losing/failing. It was just me, as Edith, exploring the lives of her family members. Some of them were very very sad, and you knew it was coming, you just didnt know how, and that was really nice.

It's a game you can enjoy on a weekend to relax as you go through each family member's life. I loved going through each room and seeing who they were, how their personalities were, as I guessed how they died before I read the diaries/poems/etc. Best to play not expecting anything, go in blind, and enjoy the ride.

I definitely liked how beautiful the game was even when it was released in 2017 (it's almost 10 years), and I could look into the forests, or the night's sky, and just relax while enjoying the story being told. HOWEVER, I did get motion sickness a few times, so if you're sensitive to it, please keep that in mind. It's still playable, but you can forgive yourself if you had to look away or take a break.

Overall, love the scenes, love the story, love the music (I absolutely made the frog swim and dance to the music while sobbing in the bathtub because I know what happens next).
I've never cried at a video game before but this game brought genuine tears to my face. this is one of those indie games that i feel like many people need to experience.

I've played a lot of story rich games in my life, but this was different. Very creative storytelling. The unique way each story is told is different from anything I've ever seen before. The art style and detailed atmosphere are also breathtakingly beautiful. My only caveat is that it is indeed a short game.
There is nothing to dislike about this game, it is one of the few games that I would say is a masterpiece, truly it's a 10/10 of a game.

I wasn't too sure whether I'd like the game or not when coming into it, but I soon found myself enjoying it more than I'd anticipated. It has great writing, a wonderful atmosphere, and I don't want to spoil anything, but I will say I love the story and want to leave it at that. The game is a bit short, but that's what I enjoyed about it (and don't worry, it doesn't rush the game towards the end of it). Overall, I highly recommend this game, 10/10.

This is by far one of my favorite games of all time- I try to get anyone who will indulge me to play it! It is both visually and thematically gorgeous.
I highly recommend going in blind, without spoilers, and playing it more than once; because what makes this game a genuine piece of art, is that it is what the individual player makes of it. You leave feeling fulfilled, introspective, maybe a little melancholic, and ultimately better off for having the experience!

went in expecting just a story game, came out thinking about my own life a bit more. each story is unique and quietly emotional in its own way. it’s short, but it sticks with you after finishing. definitely worth playing. 10/10

An AMAZING game. About the depth and breadth of living a merely human life. About choices made and internal perspectives. About things that may not even exist without our belief in them (there's more than one). The way that our homes mirror our selves, or our mysteries.

You will love Edith Finch. The Game, the character. Not just her story, but the fact that she has to know ALL the stories.
And so will you.

Play this game. Highest recommend possible. Play to find out what happens (well, happened).

A beautiful game, perfect pacing, and an outstanding way of using videogames to tell a story. This is one of those great representations of 'videogames as art' and it goes out of its way to make you as involved as you can with the story. There's not much else to say, experience it for yourself.

overall i give this game a 10/10

what remains of edith finch is genuinely one of the most emotional and memorable story-driven games i've ever played. every chapter tells a different story in a unique way, and the variety in the gameplay keeps the experience engaging from start to finish. it's the kind of game that stays with you long after the credits roll.

what makes the game so special is its storytelling. each member of the finch family has their own unforgettable story, and the atmosphere, music, and environmental details all come together perfectly. while it's not a long game, every moment feels meaningful and carefully crafted.

for the price you pay, i think it is absolutely worth it, especially if you enjoy narrative-focused games. it's an experience rather than a challenge, and it's one i would recommend to anyone who appreciates amazing storytelling in game form.

Definitely not much of a game, mostly a walking simulator with some extra interactions here and there. That having been said, it's an absolutely beautiful experience full of wonder and tragedy. Highly recommended if you're up for something like that. One playthrough takes about 2 1/2 hours and their really isn't any replay value aside from wanting to experience it again though, so keep that in mind.

A short walking simulator, but a good short walking simulator.
A lot of different artistic take providing different perspectives.
Great storytelling game, with a somewhat creepy atmosphere. Something you can pick up and struggle to stop playing until you complete all the main stories!

tldr.text: Very Positive (94%): players love the story and characters, with 71% of reviews praising them.
The main complaint is the story, which some find disappointing, and the short, light gameplay.

details.text: Story complaints are less common lately, at 7% of recent reviews against 10% of all reviews.
Newer players are the least positive, while players past 50 hours are the most positive.
